name: The Nerve Agents
label: Revelation
lede: Eric Ozenne named a band after the chemical weapons he'd trained against in the Marines, put eyeliner on Bay Area hardcore, and quit at the top. His daughter Grace was born two weeks later.

eras.title: One show, then Los Angeles
eras.text: Eric Ozenne of Redemption 87 and Unit Pride had about six months left in San Francisco before a planned move south. The band he started to fill them had a Revelation deal before they ran out.

years.big: The name was purposely to break in a different direction
q: The name was purposely to break in a different direction
years.h: A Marine names his band after what he trained against
years.p: At a Gilman Street show, Ozenne asks Andy Granelli of Model American if he's ready to start a band. Ozenne meant to play one show before leaving for LA.
years.xp:
Ozenne served in the Marine Corps infantry from 1991 to 1994 and went through chemical warfare training, which is where nerve agents come in. He says the name stuck because of how frightening they sounded.

Granelli had been pushing him to start something for a while, and helped recruit bassist Matt Sweirs and guitarist Kevin Cross. The band's first show came about two months later, at Bottom of the Hill in San Francisco.

years.h: Producer Paul Miner plays the demo for Revelation, and the phone rings
years.p: Miner records the demo at Cold Front Records in May. He passes it to Revelation co-founder Jordan Cooper, and the label signs the band.
years.xp: Ozenne had wanted to be on Revelation since meeting Walter Schriefels at 16. In his words, Miner played the tape for Cooper "and next thing you know, I get a call."

years.p: Eight songs of fast, yelled San Francisco hardcore. The EP goes out of print and stays off vinyl for more than 25 years.

eras.title: Eyeliner and the White Owl
eras.text: A new bassist brought piano, and the band put on eyeliner, pulling Siouxsie and the Banshees and 45 Grave into hardcore. Shows got frenzied and sometimes violent, and punk and hardcore kids ended up in the same room.

years.cap: Eric Ozenne singing in the crowd
q: We wanted everyone there to know that we welcomed everyone
years.src: No Echo: Eric Ozenne (Unit · Wikipedia: The Nerve Agents
years.h: Dante Sigona joins on bass, and the eyeliner goes on
years.p: Bassist Matt Sweirs leaves and Sigona takes over. The band's sound darkens toward [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]], [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] and Siouxsie.
years.xp: Ozenne has said the eyeliner was a statement against hardcore purists, a way of telling everyone at the show they were welcome. The Wikipedia entry notes theatrical costumes and a guest performer called the White Owl.

years.h: Andy Ernst records Days of the White Owl in Hayward
years.p: The Nerve Agents cut the album in November at Art of Ears, Hayward, California.

years.h: Kill Your Idols and The Nerve Agents split a Mankind record
years.p: The Nerve Agents share the record with Long Island's [[Kill Your Idols|b6154aed-416f-43bf-93fe-0906b051535f]]. Sessions Records also gathers early songs as The Way It Should Be...

years.src: Wikipedia: Days of the White Owl
yt: Full set, Gilman Street, Berkeley, Aug 2000
years.p: Sixteen songs, most under two and a half minutes, with piano pieces by Dante Sigona at both ends. [[Davey Havok|0d7bf43a-d747-4c8b-bc4c-927d9a7fe03a]] of [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]] guests, and Evil is a [[45 Grave|337027f4-4f29-42f4-bc4d-63e7d4e74e1a]] cover.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia some critics knocked the album for a lack of originality, but hardcore and punk fans took to its speed and hooks.

years.cap: Eric Ozenne on the floor with the crowd, c. 2000
years.src: No Echo: Eric Ozenne on · Wikipedia: The Nerve Agents
years.h: On the road with AFI, Agnostic Front and The Business
years.p: The Nerve Agents tour California and the East Coast with [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]], then the Spirit of the Streets tour with F-Minus, [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]] and The Business. They also play dates with [[T.S.O.L.|e3207b63-ab05-42bc-924e-b1299b89c406]]
years.xp:
Long Beach's PCH Club became a second home. Ozenne calls it a "little, tiny, hole in the wall building" that the band packed.

Bay Area shows put punk and hardcore audiences on one floor, which they usually didn't share. Wikipedia describes the sets as frenzied, chaotic and often violent.

eras.title: Out on a high note
eras.text: Tim Armstrong's Hellcat put out the second album with Epitaph handling distribution, and the crowds kept growing. Inside the band, Ozenne and Sigona had stopped agreeing.

years.cap: The bassist in a striped shirt and Eric Ozenne in a packed hall
yt: Full set, the Rotunda, Philadelphia, Aug 8, 2001
years.p: Back at Art of Ears with Andy Ernst, the band writes angular, melodic songs, mostly under two minutes. [[Jade Puget|535ae49b-d6a5-4527-a375-3a7d96022194]] of AFI sings backing vocals on one. Punknews and AllMusic each give it 2.5 stars.

years.big: Some things were said and some sides were taken and then I quit
q: Probably best that we went out on a high note.
years.src: No Echo: Eric Ozenne on · No Echo: Eric Ozenne (Unit · Wikipedia: The Nerve Agents
years.h: The Nerve Agents play their last show at The Pound
years.p: Ozenne gives an ultimatum over Dante Sigona. The band plays five December shows with [[Lars Frederiksen and the Bastards|f3a090bf-6173-42d7-86f5-7fcdeaabfc58]] and ends at The Pound in San Francisco on December 30.
years.xp:
Ozenne lost his voice during those last shows, and the crowd sang for him. His daughter Grace was born two weeks after the breakup, and he says fatherhood came first.

Wikipedia adds that Granelli's commitments to The Distillers and Ozenne's coming fatherhood played into the split.

eras.title: The Distillers and White Fence
eras.text: The members scattered into some of the better-known bands of the next decade.

years.h: Granelli lands in The Distillers, Presley in White Fence
years.p: Drummer Andy Granelli joins [[The Distillers|d25fa5a6-92bf-46a3-8bf7-31149b62eb84]] and, with guitarist Tim Presley, starts [[Darker My Love|15c5c0de-b8ff-49ab-8a58-506c89453f03]]. Presley later forms [[White Fence|68548de4-c045-426a-9745-b52a8a22d2d2]].

eras.title: Reissues, not reunions
eras.text: Revelation brought the whole catalog back, Hellcat album included. The band stayed broken up.

years.src: No Echo: Eric Ozenne on · No Echo: Eric Ozenne (Unit
years.h: Revelation puts all three Nerve Agents records back in print
years.p: Revelation's Adam Lentz pitched anniversary reissues around 2020, and Epitaph licensed The Butterfly Collection for three years. The 1998 EP gets its first vinyl pressing.
years.xp:
The reissues came out May 16, 2025, with new obi strips and expanded booklets that include contributions from the band's community.

A reunion looks unlikely. Ozenne says guitarist Tim Presley isn't a fan of reunions, and that if Presley changed his mind, he'd be all for it.
